checks_run.procedure: Try to show what D-219 does not cover: a reader learning a restricted id it could not otherwise obtain through the audit trail, the grant register, or the phase-step evidence remove echo. Read removePhaseStepEvidence and listPhaseStepEvidence (phase-steps.ts 918-1100), the sweep's ID_REF_ALLOWED and its leak check, and run the D-218 network probe (QA-R7-11).
checks_run.command: Code reading in clone r7; zz-qa-dg6r7-id-refs-network.spec.ts
checks_run.environment: Clone r7; demo stack
checks_run.expected: No undisclosed path, or a finding
checks_run.actual: No undisclosed disclosure found. The remove echo needs a link id and the link's If-Match version. The list hides a link to restricted evidence, so a step owner who is not admitted can get the link id only from the audit trail, whose events also keep the evidence item's own record id (D-219 item 1, ADR-0051 §2 'record id and versions remain'). The echo therefore reveals nothing that path does not already give. The sweep allows hidden ids only in the recordId field of the four named audit and grant operations, so 'changes' bodies that would name a hidden id fail the sweep, and it passes in both runs. One observation, not a disclosure: a not-admitted step owner holding the link id can still remove a link to restricted evidence (the remove path has no reach check). The link is kept as history and the evidence item is untouched, so this is an access-design question for the orchestrator, not a D-218/D-219 leak. I raise no finding.
